basis: RAS/MAPK developmental syndromes commonly affect neurodevelopment, heart and skin; additional organ damage varies substantially across subtypes.
Periostosis, osteitis and arthropathy define the disease; associated pulmonary or cardiac diseases are underlying conditions.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma affects hematopoietic and lymphoid tissues; lymphoma warrants the immune axis.
Gonadal differentiation and reproductive anatomy disorder; the supplied findings do not establish endocrine hormone deficiency.
Congenital abdominal wall closure defect; herniated viscera do not by themselves establish intrinsic intestinal or hepatic damage.
KISS1-related gonadotropin deficiency causes hypogonadism; neurologic injury or anosmia is not established in the supplied phenotype.
Symptomatic centronuclear skeletal myopathy; respiratory muscle weakness does not itself establish intrinsic pulmonary disease.
The concept and its parent define a bone disorder; no additional organ involvement is established.
Immune-mediated hypersensitivity inflammation of the cornea and conjunctiva; microbial antigens do not establish a separate systemic infection.
KRT4-related oral mucosal leukokeratosis; oral lesions occur in 8/8 patients. The skin-disorder ancestry does not establish cutaneous involvement.
Fusion of the atlas and axis is a structural cervical skeletal abnormality; neurologic damage is not inherent.
Muscle-tendon shortening and joint contractures define this distal arthrogryposis; trismus reflects musculoskeletal restriction.
Congenital cleft of the uvula, part of the oral soft palate; nasal speech does not establish airway damage.
Peripheral nerve injury caused by uremia; renal failure is the underlying separately diagnosed disease, not damage caused by the neuropathy.
Severe intellectual disability, regression and progressive joint contractures define the syndrome; macroglossia alone does not establish gastrointestinal dysfunction.
Defined as KIF5A-related nervous system disease; the included spastic paraplegia, neuropathy and neonatal myoclonus are neurologic.
HSF4-related nonsyndromic cataract affects the ocular lens.
Hereditary fibrous overgrowth of the gingiva; gums belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Diffuse glial neoplasm infiltrating the brain, sometimes extending into the spinal cord; all are within the neurologic axis.
Brain midline malformations and pituitary anomalies define the GLI2 phenotype; panhypopituitarism is reported in 3/11. Facial dysmorphism alone adds no axis.
Teratoma arising from the stomach; tissue components within a teratoma do not establish disease of other organs.
GPI-anchor biosynthesis disorder with intellectual disability and seizures; distal phalangeal shortening occurs in 80-99%. Renal and ocular abnormalities are only occasional.
Defining ectodermal defects affect enamel, nails and sweat glands; dental and cutaneous abnormalities occur in 80-99%.
Benign neoplasm arising in male breast parenchyma; breast has no axis.
Apical lung carcinoma; direct brachial plexus invasion causes neuropathy in roughly 30-50%. Rib invasion is variable and omitted.
